sources.title: Schematron V2 Turbo | AI Models | Inference.net
sources.evidence: Exact Turbo page gives nominal 3B and Schematron membership. Its serialized state identifies inference-net/schematron-v2-turbo, contextSize/maxContextSize 128000, reasoningSupported false, toolsSupported false, text input/output, and releaseDate 2026-04-16. It references the inaccessible Granite-named repository. Direct HTML retrieval succeeded using a standard browser User-Agent after an initial 403. Freshly reopened the exact page and full serialized product state on October 27: nominal 3B is explicit, but no active count or base_model field is present. The Granite string is only a huggingFaceId.

sources.title: Schematron V2: Frontier HTML-to-JSON extraction at a fraction of the cost
sources.evidence: Dated April 16, 2026; explicitly releases V2 Small and V2 Turbo that day. Both have 128K context and closed weights available through the serverless API. Separately labels V1 3B/8B and V2 Small/Turbo in comparisons. No production-layer architecture or active count is provided. Fresh October 27 read also confirms the pricing paragraph explicitly calls this V2 3B Turbo. This is sufficient nominal-total evidence without a tensor census; no activated-parameter count or unchanged named-base relationship is stated.

sources.title: Schematron - Inference.net Documentation
sources.evidence: Current documentation names the Turbo API identifier, gives a 128K request limit, and describes HTML plus schema as input and conforming JSON as output. V1 identifiers now route to V2, but the downloadable V1 weights remain separate models. Fresh October 27 full read again distinguishes retired V1 identifiers from V2 successors. Routing old requests to Turbo does not establish unchanged weights or inherited active parameters.

sources.title: Use Inference.net Models in Coding Agents
sources.evidence: Explicitly says inference-net/schematron-* extraction models do not support tool calls. It also documents the public model-list endpoint and its reasoning_efforts field.

sources.title: Reasoning - Inference.net Documentation
sources.evidence: Explains that models absent from its effort table have no first-party effort dial and parameter behavior is not guaranteed. Schematron is absent. This does not establish absence of all internal reasoning or an exact-model non-reasoning declaration.

sources.title: Terms of Service | Inference.net
sources.evidence: Service terms grant limited, revocable access, reserve ungranted rights, and restrict redistribution and reverse engineering. Together with the explicit closed-weight launch statement, this supports the descriptive proprietary classification.

sources.title: Schematron V2 Turbo linked Hugging Face repository
sources.evidence: Official product state and OpenRouter link this identifier. Page and unauthenticated Hugging Face API requests returned HTTP 401. No model card, configuration, weights, or license was inspected; the repository name alone cannot verify Granite ancestry or architecture. October 27 recheck of the raw README and exact model API again returned 401; no hidden card or architecture was accessed.

sources.title: Inference.net public Hugging Face model list
sources.evidence: Public list exposes Schematron-3B and Schematron-8B as the Schematron checkpoints; no V2 Turbo checkpoint was returned. This is corroboration of the developer statement, not independent proof that no private repository exists.

sources.title: OpenRouter public model API
sources.evidence: Exact Turbo listing gives context_length 128000 and text-to-text modalities, with the inaccessible Granite-named Hugging Face identifier. September 12 created timestamp is a provider-listing date, not the developer release. Catalog data is only corroborative or a discovery lead.

sources.title: HTML-to-JSON Extraction API: Extract Typed Data from Messy Web Pages
sources.evidence: June 14, 2026 guide compares exact Small and Turbo identifiers and their extraction quality/throughput. It does not disclose Turbo architecture or active parameters. This later exact-variant comparison was checked before recording those fields as undisclosed. Freshly read the complete later guide October 27. Exact Small/Turbo comparisons cover extraction quality, throughput and routing; no numerical active-count convention or model lineage is supplied.

sources.title: Hybrid-Attention models are the future for SLMs
sources.evidence: November 2025 research discusses adapting Nemotron Nano v2 and its Mamba-2/Transformer structure for specialized tasks. It never identifies Schematron V2 Turbo, so these architecture and size details are not transferred to this record. Freshly reread the full original research post October 27. Its explicit Nemotron fine-tuning relationship concerns a separate summarization experiment and supplies no Schematron Turbo ancestry.

sources.title: Inference.net public model-list API
sources.evidence: Successful unauthenticated response for the exact inference-net/schematron-v2-turbo identifier gives context_length 128000, max_completion_tokens 8192, and text input/output. No reasoning_efforts array is present. A browser User-Agent resolved the initial 403; no generation request was made. Fresh October 27 unauthenticated response again identifies the exact Turbo endpoint but includes no parameter count, active-count convention or base checkpoint.

sources.title: Linked V2 Turbo raw model-card recheck
sources.evidence: Fresh unauthenticated October 27 raw-card request returned HTTP 401, as did the exact Hugging Face model API. No card, base-model metadata or configuration was available. Repository naming remains a lead, not documented unchanged Granite lineage.

sources.title: Puter Schematron V2 Turbo serving page
sources.evidence: Freshly read the full exact Turbo page October 27. It repeats the 3B total and original extraction metrics but publishes no active count or Turbo base model. A related-model section claims a Llama 3.2 base for Small only; that unsourced sibling statement cannot establish Turbo lineage. Its September provider-listing date is not adopted as the developer launch date.

sources.title: Vercel exact Schematron V2 Turbo serving specification
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the original provider page during exact-model comparison searches. It supplies BF16 format, API limits and throughput but no total/active decomposition or named base. Weight format and serving speed cannot establish active parameters.

name.note: Exact product and launch names agree.

developer.note: Developer explicitly identified; preserve existing brand spelling.

release_date.note: Dated announcement says both V2 variants are available that day; later provider listings are not the initial release.

open_weights.note: Explicitly closed at launch; current public repository inventory reveals only V1 Schematron checkpoints. No subsequent V2 weight release was located.

license.note: Descriptive API-only classification; no open weight license is established.

parameters_b.note: Developer-reported nominal 3B total, freshly reconfirmed October 27 on the exact product page and explicit V2 3B Turbo launch-pricing text. Retain the supported nominal size; no exact tensor census is needed or asserted.

active_parameters_b.note: October 27 fresh exact Turbo name/ID searches separately checked total, active, activated, later original research and comparison sources, including arXiv and Hugging Face. Reopened the exact product HTML/state, launch, current API/docs, complete later extraction guide and developer hybrid research. None publishes an active-count convention. The linked Granite-named repository remains inaccessible and its identifier alone does not document unchanged-base lineage. V1 routing, unrelated Nemotron research and a third-party statement about sibling Small cannot transfer a count. Keep null rather than equating active with the nominal total or serving speed.

architecture.note: No exact-model architecture disclosure found in launch, current documentation, later comparisons, or searched training/interpretability research. Inaccessible repository naming and unrelated hybrid research cannot establish it.

context_window.note: Exact official API and product serialized state both give 128000 tokens. This resolves the visible page's 128K intro versus 125K detail-widget formatting.

modalities.note: Documented input is HTML text plus JSON Schema; output is JSON text.

reasoning.note: Exact Turbo serialized product object explicitly sets reasoningSupported:false and its page capabilities set reasoning:false; no reasoning_efforts appear in its official API record. This is advertised capability, not a claim about all internal computation.

tool_call.note: Exact Turbo product state sets toolsSupported:false; documentation explicitly excludes inference-net/schematron-* extraction models.

description.value: A 3B HTML-to-JSON extraction model in the Schematron family, optimized for throughput and guided by a supplied JSON Schema.
description.note: Replace unsupported general assistance and routine automation characterization with the documented specialized task.

patch.description: A 3B HTML-to-JSON extraction model in the Schematron family, optimized for throughput and guided by a supplied JSON Schema.

sources.label: Schematron V2 Turbo official model page

patch.notes: The developer reports a nominal 3B total. No separate active-parameter count or verified base-model lineage was found in the checked primary sources. V2 Turbo is API-only and distinct from open V1 checkpoints. Official API and product state confirm 128000 context, text input/output, and no reasoning or tool-calling capability.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit reconfirms nominal 3B total from the exact developer page and launch text. Fresh original-source, later-comparison and named-base searches establish no active count; explicitly patch it to null. The inaccessible Granite-named repository and V1 routing do not prove unchanged lineage. All twelve nonparameter assessments are preserved; no weights were downloaded.
